run_windows.window_rule: A window opens at a Sound_PlayBGM dispatch and closes at the next ROM epoch that replaces the music track RAM wholesale: either another Sound_PlayBGM dispatch, which reloads the tracks through InitMusicPlayback (s1.sounddriver.asm:1498-1502), or cfFadeInToPrevious, the E4 flag ending a 1-up jingle, which restores the interrupted song from v_1up_ram_copy and issues no request of its own (:2166-2223). The invocation carrying the boundary is discarded, because the ROM has already swapped the RAM before that invocation finishes walking its tracks. Each window is single-song by construction, which is what lets the reference normalize against one song's ROM asset range and the engine host drive one music sequencer.
run_windows.subset_rule: Every distinct song a movie plays is published from that movie, so a song appearing in both recordings is covered from both; the remaining budget goes to the request-dense windows. Windows containing a re-entered UpdateMusic invocation are excluded, because the ROM's partial-then-resumed track walk is not representable at invocation granularity. Red windows are published deliberately: a window with its frontier recorded pins where the engine stops agreeing. See docs/status/audio-frontier-log.md.
run_windows.regeneration: Every window in each movie's plan below is regenerable by re-running the recorder probe over that movie with OGGF_AUDIO_WINDOWS set to its ordinal. Every window is opened, walked and reported on every run; the selection only decides which are written to disk. Ordinals after a run's first 1-up restore shift by one per restore relative to a survey taken before that boundary existed, so cite a window's epoch frame alongside its ordinal.
run_windows.provenance: Two serial BizHawk captures of the whole movie per published window, verified byte-identical with cmp before anything was gzipped into the fixture tree. Windows 59 and 83 come from a second pair of whole-movie passes, since the first pair's selection list predated the 1-up restore boundary that shifted their ordinals.

s1-complete-run.plan_source: the completed whole-movie capture, so it carries the 1-up restore boundary; ordinals here supersede the pre-fix survey's, which had one fewer window
